description:
Stand where you will shoot, point your iPhone at the sky, and see exactly where the sun and the moon will be at any hour of any day. All of it computed on the device, with no account and no connection.

FOUR VIEWS, ONE PLACE AND DATE
Sky. The background is a readout, not decoration: it comes from the real solar altitude at that moment, so night is navy, twilight violet, noon pale blue. The day's arc crosses it with the sun and the moon at their true positions. Drag the time scrubber and the whole screen moves through the day, with azimuth, altitude, the next event and its countdown below.

AR. Hold the phone up and the sun and moon paths lie over the live camera, marked hour by hour, with the summer solstice, winter solstice and equinox paths behind them. In August you can see where the light falls in December. When the sky is dark enough, the galactic plane of the Milky Way joins them. A chip in the corner gives the heading accuracy in degrees and turns amber when the compass needs calibrating. Naming that uncertainty is part of the tool.

Map. Sunrise and sunset direction rays from the pin, the moon's rays beside them, the day's path over the terrain, and the shadow of an object whose height you set. Tap anywhere and every other view follows.

Data. All three twilights: civil, nautical, astronomical. Solar noon, day length, and how much the day grew or shrank since yesterday. A moon phase calendar. Eclipses with the circumstances at your own spot. The altitude curve across the year. Export to CSV or image.

YOUR REAL HORIZON
A flat horizon is a fiction wherever there are hills or buildings. Sweep the skyline with the camera and Sunlit keeps it as 36 sectors, then gives the sunrise and sunset you will really see.

WHAT IS FREE
Today, where you are standing, in all four views, free forever. Sun position and compass, the AR sun path, sunrise and sunset, all three twilights, golden hour and blue hour, solar noon, day length, shadow length, and today's UV index and irradiance as a clear sky model.

SUNLIT PRO, ONE PAYMENT
Not a subscription. Nothing renews.
• Any date, past or future
• Saved places and any point on earth
• The moon: phase, path, rise, set, distance, calendar
• The Milky Way: galactic centre, galactic plane, and a visibility window that names its limiting factor
• Annual path overlay with solstice and equinox curves
• Your measured horizon and the obstruction periods it produces
• Eclipses with local circumstances
• Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets
• Event notifications
• CSV and image export

HOW ACCURATE
Solar position comes from the NREL Solar Position Algorithm, accurate to 0.0003 degrees. Lunar position comes from a truncated ELP-2000/82 series, accurate to about 10 arcseconds. Rise, set and twilight times come from a numerical solver rather than an interpolation, so high latitudes and grazing events come out right, and polar day and polar night are reported as such rather than an invented time.

UV index and irradiance are CLEAR SKY MODELS. They are computed from geometry and an ozone climatology, not measured, and carry that label everywhere they appear. Cloud changes what actually reaches you.

PRIVACY
No account, no email address, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking. Nothing you enter leaves your iPhone, and all the astronomy runs with no connection at all. The Map view loads Apple Maps tiles, which need a connection like any map; the rays and paths on top do not.

whatsNew:
First release.

Sunlit computes the sun, the moon and the centre of the Milky Way on your iPhone, for any date and any place, with no account and no connection.

Four views: Sky, AR, Map and Data. Today, at your current location, is free in all four and stays free.
